topic.symptom: After adding or moving memory, the PC powers on but does not boot to a picture.
topic.title: Added RAM, Now It Won't Boot? Check It's Fully Seated

script: Added RAM, now it won't boot? Shut it down and unplug it first. Check that each stick is fully seated. Line up the notch with the slot. Press firmly until the clips snap shut. Plug it back in. Then try booting again.

storyboard.title: Added RAM, Now It Won't Boot? Check It's Fully Seated
storyboard.narrationStyle: Calm, conversational, one check. The captions are burned into the cut; no voice generated.

beats.narration: Added RAM, now it won't boot?
beats.visualDirection: The stylized PC powers on (fans light) beside a monitor that stays dark.

beats.narration: Shut it down and unplug it first.
beats.visualDirection: A second press shuts it down and the fans slow to a stop; at the back, the power cord comes out of the power supply.

beats.narration: Check that each stick is fully seated.
beats.visualDirection: The glass side panel slides off; the camera closes on the four memory slots; one stick is outlined: not fully in.

beats.narration: Line up the notch with the slot.
beats.visualDirection: Side view of the slot: guides through the stick's notch and the slot's ridge turn green as they line up; the stick goes in.
beats.onScreenText: SIDE VIEW OF THE SLOT → LINE UP THE NOTCH

beats.narration: Press firmly until the clips snap shut.
beats.visualDirection: Thumbs press the stick down; the clips at both ends snap shut; the stick sits level, outlined in green.
beats.onScreenText: FIRM, EVEN PRESSURE → CLIPS SNAP SHUT → FULLY SEATED

beats.visualDirection: Back on the board, all sticks level; the panel slides back on; at the back, the cord goes back in.
The unlit PC beside the dark monitor, its power button pulsing amber. No one presses it; no boot is shown.

factualGuardrails: Never say: always the sole culprit behind boot failures (A PC can fail to boot for many reasons; seating is one check.)
Never say: guaranteed cure for boot failures (It may not work; the Short offers a check, never a guaranteed fix.)
Never say: successfully boots straight into Windows afterwards (The cut ends before anyone presses the button; no boot is shown or promised.)
persistentDisclosures: Stylized example · not a fix for every PC

mechanism.why: no trusted approval record exists in this repository: a caller-supplied reviewer name and time is recorded, but does not prove anyone watched or listened, so it cannot close the gate. A decision is recorded with the bytes and cut it names; an approval never closes a gate, and a recorded rejection always blocks.

Is the factual takeaway understood correctly, with no misleading emphasis, after one watch?
Are all text, numbers and game names readable at real size, inside the visible area?
Is the pacing intentional: no rushed line, no dead air, and every cut lands on its line?
Does the style suit a beginner choosing a gaming PC?
After a full listen: is every word pronounced correctly, and is the mix clear?
Is each disclosure understandable in context, while the claim it qualifies is on screen?
Are the rights to every asset signed off, and is publication of this exact cut authorised?
